provenance.citation: Gao J., Shi N., Li Y., Jiang B., Marhaba T., Zhang W., Electrocatalytic Upcycling of Nitrate Wastewater into an Ammonia Fertilizer via an Electrified Membrane, Environ. Sci. Technol. 56 (2022) 11602-11613
provenance.figure: Fig. 3d (stacked bars, N concentration vs time in hours, real wastewater; journal p. 11608, PDF page 7; this dataset keeps the 0-180 min DC-on period)
provenance.file: publisher PDF via NSF PAR record 10451706 (par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10451706); local copy 10451706.pdf, not committed
provenance.notes: Two-compartment system. The cathode loop (feed tank <-> cathode chamber, 50 mL/min) holds NO3-, NO2- and TAN ('TAN in feed tank' / 'TAN in reaction chamber' -> species NH3). Gaseous NH3 crosses the hydrophobic PTFE membrane into the trap chamber, whose 0.5 M Na2SO4 is recirculated (50 mL/min) through the trap chamber, the anode chamber (acidified by O2 evolution; Nafion 117 PEM between cathode and anode chambers) and the trap tank, where NH3 is held as NH4+ ('TAN in trap tank/chamber' -> species NH3_trap, kept separate, never added to NH3). Fig. 1a and Fig. S2a also show an air pump on the wastewater tank and a 'gaseous NH3' line from the wastewater tank to the trap tank, so NH3 may also reach the trap by headspace stripping; the text does not quantify that route. N2 was not measured: the authors computed it as initial N minus (NO3- + NO2- + TAN in both tanks) (SI Part S2) and plotted it as the top bar segment; it is stored as quality.reported_n_loss, not as a species, and our n_closure is 1 minus that gap. NO and N2O were assumed negligible by the authors (SI Part S2), not measured. METHOD: Raster digitization of the embedded Fig. 3 image (main PDF page 7, 2092x976 px, 300 ppi) (the figures are embedded raster images; there are no vector paths). Image extracted at native resolution with pdfimages; y axis calibrated by a linear fit to tick-mark pixel centroids located automatically (darkness profile beside the axis line) and assigned to the printed tick labels (all labelled and minor ticks, >=4 per panel, max tick residual <0.15 of one minor step); bars located at the x tick centroids. For each bar two side strips (avoiding the centred error bars and the outline) were classified pixel-wise by nearest colour prototype, the two orange TAN classes split by hue; segment boundaries come from a monotone dynamic-programming segmentation that enforces the legend's stacking order. Resolution 0.096 mM per pixel; boundary uncertainty about +/-1-2 px. Segments not visible are recorded as 0.0 (below ~1 px); values below ~0.2 mM (<=2-3 px) cannot be distinguished from outline/anti-aliasing artefacts. Error bars in the figure were not extracted. Extracted by agent team 2026-10-20; overlay of the extracted boundaries on the figure crop checked by eye (scratch, not committed).  Time axis in hours; bar positions 0-5 h written as 0-300 min (x60). c0 = 436 mg/L NO3--N / 14.007 = 31.13 mM (text); the digitized t=0 bar top reads 31.18 mM. Text: rates 436 +/- 18 g-N m-2 d-1 NO3- removal, no significant NO3-, NO2- or TAN left in the feed tank after 5 h (we read 0.79 mM TAN in the feed tank at 5 h, a visible segment; the 4-5 h points are in wpd_datasets_full_0-300min.csv, not in the converted dataset). reported_n_loss is the authors' by-difference N2 (initial N minus the measured species), so besides any real N2 it carries any reading bias of the stacked-bar tops (about 0.11 mM in Fig. 2e) and absorbs any NH3 stripped from the feed tank through the air line that does not end up in the trap. Sparse: only 3 sampling times after t0 (60, 120 and 180 min) fall in the DC-on window, so the flag 'sparse' is set. Licence/terms: publisher copyright (ACS); NSF public-access copy. The PAR record (par.nsf.gov/biblio/10451706) states no reuse licence; the downloaded file is the ACS typeset article (PAR labels its full text 'Accepted Manuscript') and carries the ACS notice 'See https://pubs.acs.org/sharingguidelines for options on how to legitimately share published articles'. Checked Oct 20 2026.

conditions.catalyst: CuO-coated Cu foam (mixed-valence Cu2+/Cu1+ oxide layer) clipped to a PTFE/PP membrane (0.45 um), 4 cm2, as the electrified membrane cathode
conditions.electrolyte: real chemical-industry wastewater (Shandong Keyuan Pharmaceutical Co.): NO3--N 436 +/- 15 mg/L (31.1 mM), Br- 80 +/- 3 mg/L, Cl- 214 +/- 9 mg/L (6.0 mM), SO4 2- 106,728 +/- 918 mg/L, Na+ 19,100 +/- 523 mg/L, K+ 2447 +/- 68 mg/L, COD 140 +/- 4 mg/L, pH 2.1 +/- 0.5 (used as received)
conditions.potential_as_reported: -2.0 V vs SCE (no ohmic compensation; SCE +0.241 V vs SHE)
conditions.stirring: recirculation by peristaltic pumps at 50 mL/min (cathode loop: feed tank <-> cathode chamber; trap loop: trap tank -> trap chamber -> anode chamber -> trap tank)
conditions.notes: Three-chamber flow cell: trap | CuO@Cu-foam/PTFE cathode membrane | cathode chamber | Nafion 117 PEM | anode chamber (Pt mesh 3.5x3.5 cm); SCE reference in the cathode chamber; CHI 1100C potentiostat. volume_mL is null: the feed volume is not stated for this run (the text states a 50 mL feed tank only for the Fig. 2e synthetic run); chamber and trap-tank volumes are not stated either. pH is the initial pH of the real wastewater (2.1 +/- 0.5, used as received); in-run pH is not reported for this run. The text's in-run values, a strongly alkaline cathode loop (12.65 +/- 0.13, attributed to 'the trap chamber' in the text but in context the cathode side) and a final trap-tank pH of 1.53 +/- 0.10 after 120 min, are stated only for the 25 mM, pH 7 synthetic run of Fig. 2e. No current or current density is reported for this run; the text's ~50 mA cm-2 (0.204 +/- 0.011 A) also belongs to the Fig. 2e run, and Fig. 3b has no real-wastewater bar, so no current can be derived. RHE conversion not done: large uncompensated iR, and the in-run pH is not reported. Feed pumped at 50 mL/min through the cathode chamber and back to the feed tank; trap loop 0.5 M Na2SO4 pH 7. DC on 0-3 h, DC off 3-5 h. Powered window: this dataset (wpd_datasets.csv and data/real/gao2022_fig3d_cuo_realww.json) holds t <= 180 min only, so potential_mode 'potentiostatic' holds for every stored point. The full 0-300 min digitization (values unchanged, including the DC-off points) is kept in data/digitized_inputs/gao2022_fig3d_cuo_realww/wpd_datasets_full_0-300min.csv and is not converted. How the DC-off time was established: the text gives no switch time for this run. Fig. 3d labels 'DC on' and 'DC off' on either side of a dashed vertical line that sits midway between the 3 h and 4 h bars (pixel measurement on the native main-text image: x = 1843 px, 0.48 of the bar-centre gap), so the last DC-on sample is 3 h (180 min) and the switch fell between 3 and 4 h. Corroboration (derived): the text's NO3- removal rate (436 +/- 18 g-N m-2 d-1) equals 31.1 mM x 50 mL removed over 180 min on 4 cm2. That fits the 3-h window if the feed was 50 mL as in the synthetic runs, but the feed volume is not stated for this run (it would be 83 mL for a 5-h normalization), so the rate does not confirm the window on its own. Sampling hourly.

quality.n_basis_note: All segments, including trap TAN, are plotted on one 'N concentration (mM)' axis and stack to the initial N, and the paper's TAN recovery (Eq. S8) divides the trap-tank TAN concentration by the input nitrate concentration. That only conserves N if the trap tank volume equals the feed tank volume (feed tank 50 mL is stated; the trap tank volume is not stated) or if the authors normalized trap TAN to the feed volume. NH3_trap is therefore taken as trap-loop N per feed volume, mM-N equivalent; treat its absolute basis as unverified. NO3-, NO2-, TAN are plotted as N (axis 'N concentration'/'N species'; nitrate given as NO3--N in the text), so no N-atom conversion. No equivalent of the Fig. 2e '1.05 mmol' cross-check exists for this run: the paper states a molar amount of generated NH3 only for the Fig. 2e run (see the gao2022_fig2e_cuo_m2v n_basis_note; same cell and protocol), so the trap basis here rests on that run and on the shared Eq. S8/S9 definitions.
